rules.name: Category definition
rules.input_form: objects, morphisms, composition, identities
preconditions: Composition is associative and identities exist for each object
rules.operation: Recognize a category from its compositional data.
examples: Sets with functions form a standard category
counterexamples: A directed graph without associative composition and identities is not automatically a category

rules.name: Functor preservation rule
rules.input_form: mapping between categories
preconditions: Source and target categories are fixed
rules.operation: Verify that a candidate functor preserves identities and composition.
examples: Forgetful constructions often preserve compositional structure while discarding extra data
counterexamples: Mapping objects while breaking composition is invalid

rules.name: Natural transformation seed
rules.input_form: two functors F and G
rules.output_form: component morphisms with commuting naturality squares
preconditions: The functors share source and target categories
rules.operation: Build a natural transformation from component morphisms satisfying naturality.
examples: Canonical comparison maps between two functors are natural only when all naturality squares commute
counterexamples: Choosing unrelated component morphisms with no square compatibility is invalid

rules.name: Universal property seed
rules.input_form: candidate universal object and compatible morphisms
preconditions: The ambient diagram shape and compatibility conditions are fixed
rules.operation: Characterize an object by unique factorization of compatible morphisms.
examples: Products and coproducts are specified by their mapping universality rather than by elementwise recipes alone
counterexamples: Existence without uniqueness is insufficient for the standard universal-property pattern

rules.name: Adjunction seed
rules.input_form: functors F and G
preconditions: The relevant source and target categories are fixed
rules.operation: Recognize adjunction through natural bijections of hom-sets.
examples: Free and forgetful constructions often appear as adjoint pairs
counterexamples: Object-level correspondence without hom-set naturality is invalid

rules.name: Commutative diagram consistency rule
rules.input_form: diagram with parallel composite paths
preconditions: All named composites in the diagram are defined
rules.operation: Require all relevant composites between common endpoints to agree.
examples: Diagram commutativity encodes structural compatibility without introducing elementwise reasoning
counterexamples: Checking only one path pair in a larger diagram is insufficient in general

rules.name: Limit cone seed
rules.input_form: diagram with a candidate universal cone
rules.output_form: limit object and universal factorization property
preconditions: A diagram shape and cone compatibility conditions are fixed
rules.operation: Characterize limits by universal cones and unique factorization.
examples: Products, pullbacks, and inverse limits are organized by universal cone structure rather than by ad hoc elementwise recipes
counterexamples: A compatible cone without universal factorization is not automatically a limit

rules.name: Yoneda embedding seed
rules.input_form: object and representable hom-functor context
rules.output_form: object behavior encoded by natural transformation data
preconditions: A locally well-formed hom-functor setting is fixed
rules.operation: Use representable functors and natural transformations to encode object behavior categorically.
examples: Representable functors encode object behavior through natural transformations instead of hidden internal coordinates
counterexamples: Treating arbitrary set-valued assignments as representable is invalid

rules.name: Monoidal structure seed
rules.input_form: category with tensor product and unit data
preconditions: Tensor product, unit object, and coherence maps are fixed
rules.operation: Equip a category with associative tensor and unit structure up to coherence.
examples: Parallel composition of processes can be formalized by tensor structure rather than by overloading ordinary composition
counterexamples: Having a binary operation with no coherence data is not automatically monoidal structure

rules.name: Monad seed
rules.input_form: endofunctor with unit and multiplication candidates
preconditions: An endofunctor and natural transformation data are fixed
rules.operation: Recognize monads through unit and multiplication coherence identities.
examples: Algebraic effects and free constructions can be encoded by monadic structure instead of by one-off rewrite rules
counterexamples: An endofunctor alone is not automatically a monad

rules.name: Abelian exactness seed
rules.input_form: abelian-category style kernel, cokernel, and sequence data
preconditions: Kernel, cokernel, and additive categorical structure are fixed
rules.operation: Generalize algebraic exactness through abelian categorical structure.
examples: Categorical exactness lets diagrammatic arguments recover algebraic short-exact-sequence behavior abstractly
counterexamples: An arbitrary category with limits is not automatically abelian

rules.name: Canonical form normalization expansion
rules.input_form: raw expression E
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Rewrite expressions into a canonical form that preserves the active equivalence relation.
examples: x + y and y + x map to a shared canonical additive form in commutative settings
counterexamples: Applying canonicalization rules outside their preconditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions
